name: storage-payment-bucket-page
description: The shape of a real payment lure that saturates every category it touches (links, wording and the model) and touches nothing else. It names no brand, so no impersonation rule has anything to compare, and it sends from a throwaway domain under a real TLD whose own SPF and DKIM pass, so Gmail shows nothing for authentication to report: identity and authentication, 35 of the 100 points, are left empty by design. What it does wrong is all in links and wording: three buttons to HTML pages in one public storage bucket, a demand to update payment details, a threat to delete the account, and a forged 'trusted sender' notice. Every name, address, bucket and relay host is invented; storage.googleapis.com is kept because it is the finding.
